transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-26
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Record: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Veridian Head of AI), Marcus Delaunay (Veridian Platform Eng), Sofia Jimenez (Veridian PM)
Artifacts referenced: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/veridian-poc-v2.pdf, bench sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/veridian-bench-2025-11.xlsx, security note: s3://redwood-sec/veridian-kms-diagram.png

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick check - is this still a good 50 minutes for folks?
[00:08] Anika Rao: yeah that's fine, we have Marcus and Sofia on the line, ready to go.
[00:11] Marcus Delaunay: yup, thanks. we've got a couple infra folks in chat but not on audio.
[00:16] Maya Chen: awesome, today is mostly convergence review, we dug into the regression you flagged last week and we want to walk through the bisection results, and plan a small canary/rollout once infra is prepped. Liam, want to kick off with the quick results summary?
[00:29] Liam O'Rourke: sure, thanks. so recall the failure mode - a bump in false positives for entity extraction on the comms prompts after the prompt pruning update. we ran a diff bisection across the 4 prompt variants and 3 model quantization profiles. the high-level: variant C consistently underperformed at p95 in the headless sim, and we saw token-level hallucination spikes on long-context cases.
[01:02] Anika Rao: just to clarify, variant C is the one where we removed the clarify-step, right?
[01:06] Liam O'Rourke: exactly, the clarification micro-prompt that asked the model to confirm ambiguous acronyms. once we removed it to speed up latency we lost a guardrail.
[01:14] Sofia Jimenez: do we have numbers on latency delta when C ran vs baseline?
[01:18] Liam O'Rourke: yes, baseline p50 was 110ms, variant C p50 96ms so about 14ms improvement but p95 for baseline 320ms vs variant C 380ms in heavy context - so tail latency worsened.
[01:32] Marcus Delaunay: hmm that's interesting, short requests faster but heavy sequences got worse - likely batching or kv-cache churn? we've seen similar on our infra when KV cache warms.
[01:42] Liam O'Rourke: we thought it might be KV cache evictions, but the profile shows more repeated re-queries, leading to more decoding time. could be prompt truncation or tokenization differences.
[01:53] Maya Chen: important note - some of the transcripts from the bench run were auto-labeled and the NER tags got swapped, so take the early numbers with a grain. the bench sheet has raw logs if you want to inspect.
[02:05] Anika Rao: yeah we'll pull the raw logs. for our success criteria we have p95 generation under 400ms and entity F1 above 0.92. that F1 dip to 0.88 last week is what's worrying execs.
[02:20] Maya Chen: understood. our immediate ask is a curated regression set - Anika, you mentioned 5k prompts you can share?
[02:27] Anika Rao: yes we can hand over 5k assorted real support comms, but need to scrub PII first; timeline's Monday.
[02:33] Sofia Jimenez: we've started a light scrub but will complete by EOD Friday.
[02:37] Liam O'Rourke: perfect. once we have labelled regression set we'll run a targeted bisection that flags the exact prompt change. last run showed the prune step removing boundary clarifiers as the likely culprit.
[02:49] [03:00] -- Transcript jump --
[03:00] Marcus Delaunay: switching to infra: we wanted clarification on Redwood private vs dedicated for this POC. our security folks lean private (VPC) but we also want to understand throughput for dedicated GPUs.
[03:13] Maya Chen: good question. quick primer: Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our host env with isolation and an SLA; Redwood Private runs the control plane in our cloud but the inference plane can live in your VPC or on-prem. the private agent allows KMS integration and no egress of payloads to public tenants.
[03:33] Marcus Delaunay: and is KMS key wrapping supported with our HSM vendor? we use Thyris HSM and need envelope encryption.
[03:41] Liam O'Rourke: yes we've integrated via customer KMS + envelope. there are a few network flows to be allowed for the agent; we'll send the diagram. note: there was one customer who had to open an extra port for license handshake - we'll call that out.
[03:55] Anika Rao: and SOC2 audit logs? we need retention for 2 years and exportable events.
[04:02] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports audit export, and we can set retention policies for enterprise customers. we'll share the SOC2 appendix and audit log schema.
[04:12] Sofia Jimenez: perfect. timeline is tight - execs want a canary by Dec 10, but realistically we need dedicated infra and regression remediation first.
[04:22] Maya Chen: can we line up a 48-hour canary with 10% traffic from your staging cluster in the dev region? that gives us live traffic without full cutover.
[04:30] Marcus Delaunay: yes, staging can route that, but we need the private agent fully provisioned with KMS and allowlist before that.
[04:37] Maya Chen: understood. we'll treat the infra work as blocking for canary.
[04:41] [05:00] -- Deep dive into bisection artifacts --
[05:00] Liam O'Rourke: here's what we did: ran A/B across prompt variants, quantized int4 vs int8, and two kernel selections. notable finding: int4 with the pruning step amplified the hallucination cases on long context. int8 reduced hallucinations but increased p50 by ~30ms.
[05:25] Anika Rao: are these quantization artifacts or something with prompt formatting?
[05:29] Liam O'Rourke: likely an interaction - quantization changed token logits slightly, and the pruned prompt removed the disambiguation clause. together they push the model into a lower-confidence decode path.
[05:39] Marcus Delaunay: okay how feasible is it to run int8 in our dedicated pool? we have limited GPU memory.
[05:45] Liam O'Rourke: depends on instance type. int8 increases memory but we can also reduce batch size; Redwood Optimize can suggest a recommended config given your QPS profile. we'll run that once we have your QPS and seq length histograms.
[05:58] Sofia Jimenez: I can pull seq length histograms from our logs today.
[06:02] Maya Chen: great. next is prompt surgery: our recommendation is reintroduce a minimal clarifier but in a compact token form to balance latency. we can A/B test two clarifier lengths in canary.
[06:15] Anika Rao: would adding clarifiers at inference time hurt token cost significantly?
[06:20] Liam O'Rourke: it will add a small token overhead, but cost delta is minor compared to re-running for hallucinated corrections or human triage.
[06:28] Marcus Delaunay: cost is a concern - execs asked for a cost estimate for 100k requests/day.
[06:33] Maya Chen: we'll put that in the pricing overlay. preliminary estimate in the bench sheet shows dedicated cost about 28% lower per token at steady-state versus hosted at your QPS, but private may have infra provisioning overhead.
[06:46] [07:00] -- Security & compliance clarifications --
[07:00] Anika Rao: two security asks: 1) full TLS between agent and KMS, 2) proof of encryption at rest for intermediate caches.
[07:10] Liam O'Rourke: TLS is standard, and the KV cache can be configured to encrypt at rest; for private deployments we'll document the encryption keys lifecycle with your security team.
[07:19] Marcus Delaunay: what's in the audit logs? do they include raw prompts? if they do, we need masking.
[07:25] Maya Chen: we can mask or hash prompt payloads in logs; raw prompts can be excluded from audit exports if required. we'll include the log schema in the security pack.
[07:35] [08:00] -- Decisions and tradeoffs --
[08:00] Sofia Jimenez: to recap the tradeoffs we discussed: pruning gives lower p50 but unstable p95 and regression risk; adding a short clarifier stabilizes quality but costs tokens; quantization reduces cost but can amplify hallucinations with aggressive prompt edits.
[08:20] Maya Chen: yes exactly. recommendation is to run two parallel experiments: canary A uses int8 + minimal clarifier, canary B uses int4 + clarifier (longer) and compare with staging for 48h.
[08:35] Anika Rao: agree. and if canary A shows stable F1 and p95 under thresholds we prefer that.
[08:42] Marcus Delaunay: ok we will try that, Marcus to provision subnet and open allowlist to Redwood agent.
[08:49] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with the exact agent IPs and the minimal NACL changes in a note.
[08:54] [09:30] -- Logistics and artifacts --
[09:30] Liam O'Rourke: attaching the bisection artifacts to bench sheet - there's a folder per run and a small script to reproduce the variant test. note: some filenames got munged by auto-export (spaces-> underscores) so double-check.
[09:50] Maya Chen: action items recap — (quick): Maya will send pricing and burst doc; Liam will run targeted benchmark after Anika shares prompts; Marcus will open infra ticket; Sofia will confirm stakeholders.
[10:10] Anika Rao: timeline check: if we get prompts Monday and infra ready by Nov 30, we can do a canary first week of Dec and report back with full metrics.
[10:20] Maya Chen: sounds good. any other questions or blockers?
[10:24] Marcus Delaunay: one micro-blocker - we use a non-standard MTU and our VPN can cause packet fragmentation; will that affect agent stability?
[10:32] Liam O'Rourke: we've seen fragmentation issues before. we'll include MTU tuning notes in the infra doc; recommend GRE/UDP keepalive and path MTU discovery enabled.
[10:45] [11:30] -- Closing --
[11:30] Sofia Jimenez: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll expect the docs and the bench updates.
[11:36] Maya Chen: thanks Veronica - wait sorry, who spoke? (laughs) Anika?
[11:41] Anika Rao: that's fine, thanks Maya.
[11:43] Maya Chen: ok we'll follow up in the CRM with the deck/bench links and action items. see you next week.
[11:50] Meeting end.
